title: Extension of invertible modules from punctured local Picard triviality
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] such that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and let $Z\subseteq|X|$ be closed. For $z\in Z$ put $R_z=\mathcal O_{X,z}$ and $P_z=\operatorname{Spec}R_z\setminus\{\mathfrak m_z\}$, where $\mathfrak m_z$ is its maximal ideal [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion]. Assume $\dim R_z\ge2$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and that every invertible $\mathcal O_{P_z}$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] is trivial, for every $z\in Z$. Then for every open $H\subseteq X$ the restriction functor from invertible $\mathcal O_H$-modules to invertible $\mathcal O_{H\setminus Z}$-modules is fully faithful and essentially surjective: every such module on $H\setminus Z$ extends to $H$, and every morphism between restrictions of two invertible modules on $H$ extends uniquely. Empty $Z$ and empty $X$ are allowed.

source.place: EGA IV4 Proposition 21.13.10 together with 21.13.8 and definition 21.13.1, specialized to normal schemes and punctured-Picard triviality in local dimension >=2. Read in the online English EGA translation; local EGA IV4 WANTED.

proof.text: Fix an open $H\subseteq X$ and put $U=H\setminus Z$. Cover $H$ by normal integral affine opens $W$: first choose a Noetherian affine neighbourhood by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], then its open integral component by [rem-pc-regular-normal](2), and an affine neighbourhood inside that component. Normality and the dimension condition restrict because open subschemes have the same local rings; local Noetherianity restricts by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. For every nonempty open $T$ inside one such $W$, $T$ is integral and all points of $T\setminus U$ have local dimension at least two. An invertible module on $T$ or $T\cap U$ is coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]: its trivializations give quasi-coherence and finite type. It is reflexive since on each rank-one trivialization evaluation identifies with $\mathcal O\to\mathcal Hom(\mathcal Hom(\mathcal O,\mathcal O),\mathcal O)$, the identity under evaluation at $1$.

source.place: EGA IV4 21.13.10 converse, with 21.13.8 and 21.13.1; generic noninvertibility obstruction, implemented using Stacks Tags 0EBJ, 0AY0 and 0AY3. EGA read in the online English translation; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Let $A,B$ be two invertible modules on $H$ and $f:A|_U\to B|_U$. On each chart $W$, [lem-sfb-normal-reflexive-open-equivalence] gives a unique map $f_W:A|_W\to B|_W$ with the required restriction. On any overlap, cover by normal integral affine opens $T$ as in step 1 and apply the same Hom bijection to $T\cap U\hookrightarrow T$: the two maps agree there, hence on $T$. By morphism gluing [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules](1), they agree on the overlap and glue to a map on $H$. Uniqueness follows by the same chartwise Hom injectivity and gluing. This proves full faithfulness independently of essential surjectivity, and applies to every open subscheme of $H$.

source.place: EGA IV4 21.13.10 converse, with 21.13.8 and 21.13.1; generic noninvertibility obstruction, implemented using Stacks Tags 0EBJ, 0AY0 and 0AY3. EGA read in the online English translation; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: For an invertible module $L$ on $U$, work on a chart $W$ of step 1 and write $j:U\cap W\hookrightarrow W$. The dimension hypothesis and [lem-sfb-normal-reflexive-open-equivalence] give $F=j_*(L|_{U\cap W})$ coherent reflexive, together with $F|_{U\cap W}\simeq L|_{U\cap W}$. Let $V$ be the union of opens on which $F$ is invertible and $N=W\setminus V$. Thus $N$ is closed and lies in $Z\cap W$. If $N$ is nonempty, [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] gives an irreducible component $C$ and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober] gives its generic point $y$. Every strict generization $t$ of $y$ in $W$ lies in $V$: otherwise its irreducible closure is contained in $N$ and contains $C$, hence equals $C$ by maximality; uniqueness of its generic point forces $t=y$. The point $y\in Z$ satisfies $\dim\mathcal O_{W,y}\ge2$.

source.place: EGA IV4 21.13.10 converse, with 21.13.8 and 21.13.1; generic noninvertibility obstruction, implemented using Stacks Tags 0EBJ, 0AY0 and 0AY3. EGA read in the online English translation; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Put $R=\mathcal O_{W,y}$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $P=S\setminus\{\mathfrak m_y\}$ and $J=F_y$. The canonical map $c:S\to W$ in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism] identifies $P$ with strict generizations of $y$ and preserves their local rings. The ring $R$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], using the affine stalk description in that canonical-map node. It is a normal domain by the hypothesis on $X$, so $S$ is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field] and normal by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain]. The coherent module $F$ is quasi-coherent of finite type on the locally Noetherian $W$ by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. The module $J$ is finite and reflexive: [lem-sfb-affine-reflexive-module-comparison] gives reflexivity of this stalk; [lem-sbc-affine-module-germ-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] express it as the localization of the finite module $F(W)$, whose finitely many generators still generate after localization.

source.place: EGA IV4 21.13.10 converse, with 21.13.8 and 21.13.1; generic noninvertibility obstruction, implemented using Stacks Tags 0EBJ, 0AY0 and 0AY3. EGA read in the online English translation; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Let $E=\widetilde J$ on $S$. It is coherent reflexive by [lem-sfb-affine-reflexive-module-comparison]. Since $F$ is quasi-coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], the counit in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] identifies $F$ with $\widetilde{F(W)}$ on $W$, and the affine pullback formula [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change] identifies $c^*F$ with $\widetilde{R\otimes_{\mathcal O(W)}F(W)}=E$, since [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base], with base and algebra both $\mathcal O(W)$ and first module $\mathcal O(W)$, identifies this tensor with the localization $J$ of step 4. Every point of $P$ maps into $V$ by step 3. Pulling back a rank-one trivialization of $F|_V$ gives a rank-one trivialization of $E|_P$: in the tensor definition [def-pc-module-pullback], pullback of the structure sheaf is the structure sheaf. Thus $E|_P$ is invertible. The hypothesis of the item at $y$ gives an isomorphism $E|_P\simeq\mathcal O_P$.

source.place: EGA IV4 21.13.10 converse, with 21.13.8 and 21.13.1; generic noninvertibility obstruction, implemented using Stacks Tags 0EBJ, 0AY0 and 0AY3. EGA read in the online English translation; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normal-reflexive-open-equivalence] on $S$ with complement its closed point, whose local ring is $R$ and whose dimension is at least two. Both $E$ and $\mathcal O_S$ are coherent reflexive. The isomorphism of step 5 and its inverse extend uniquely; their composites restrict to identities, so Hom injectivity makes the composites identities. Hence $E\simeq\mathcal O_S$. Taking global sections and using the tilde unit [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] gives $J\simeq R$. The coherent module $F$ is locally finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-local-finite-presentation]. Apply [lem-trf-finite-presentation-stalk-basis-spread] at $y$ to a basis of $J$ of rank one. It gives a neighbourhood on which $F\simeq\mathcal O$, contrary to $y\in N$. Thus $N$ is empty and $F$ is invertible on all of $W$.

source.place: EGA IV4 21.13.10 converse, with 21.13.8 and 21.13.1; generic noninvertibility obstruction, implemented using Stacks Tags 0EBJ, 0AY0 and 0AY3. EGA read in the online English translation; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: We now have extensions $F_i$ on the charts $W_i$, with isomorphisms to $L$ on $U\cap W_i$. On $W_i\cap W_j$ the latter give transition isomorphisms over $U$; by full faithfulness from step 2 they extend uniquely to maps $F_i\to F_j$ on the overlap. Extend their inverses too; uniqueness forces their composites to be identities. The triple cocycle follows by the same uniqueness from its equality on $U$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules](2) to obtain a module on $H$. It is invertible by [def-sc-invertible-module], since it is so on each chart. The chosen isomorphisms to $L$ agree with the transitions and glue, using clause (1) of the same node, to an isomorphism of its restriction with $L$. If $H$ is empty the empty cover gives the unique module. If $Z$ is empty take $L$ itself. A nonempty integral chart cannot be contained in $Z$, since its generic point has dimension zero. This also deals with the possible empty opens without imposing density as an extra hypothesis.
